title: Getting the units right
summary: rad/s to rotations per second to volts to duty cycle.

say.never: Numbers in robot code come in different units, and they have to be converted. The target is in radians per second, but kV wants rotations per second, and the motor wants a duty cycle. Each line on the board converts one unit into the next, like converting inches to feet to yards.
say.bit: The target is in radians per second, kV wants rotations per second, and the motor wants a duty cycle.

board.code:
double rps = CONSTANTS.SHOOT_VELOCITY / (2 * Math.PI);   // rad/s -> rotations/s
double volts = CONSTANTS.FLYWHEEL_KV * rps;              // what it takes to hold that speed
double duty = volts / 12.0;                              // a fraction of the battery

say.never: Here's the sneaky part: a wrong unit doesn't crash anything. The robot just does the wrong thing, quietly. So write the unit next to every number you can, in a comment or the variable's name.
say.bit: A wrong unit doesn't crash: it just makes the robot do the wrong thing. Write the unit next to every number you can.
